newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinians launch firm to buy Jerusalem land.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians launch firm to buy Jerusalem land.

text.p: Palestinian businessmen on Saturday launched a multi-million dollar firm to buy and develop land in East Jerusalem, saying the aim was to block further Israeli takeovers of Arab land from Palestinians.
Banker Abdul-Majid Shoman told a meeting of investors the company, which hoped to raise $500 million, would counterbalance Jewish funds that promote Israeli projects in Jerusalem.

"We aspire that Arab money will have its influential role in the preservation of Arab property and Arab presence in this holy city and stop its Judaisation," Shoman, chairman of Jordan's heavyweight Arab Bank, told investors.

The holding company, whose offshore registration is expected within a month, would invest in real estate, commercial and industrial ventures and provide legal advisory services for Jerusalem's Arab residents to help protect and develop their property against Israeli takeover.
Shoman, one of three businessmen behind the idea, said he hoped the company's capital would reach at least $500 million as the organisers began lobbying Arab investors and institutions.
Investors behind the project said all the funds would operate on a sound financial profit basis with many opportunities available in the holy city.
Shoman appealed to investors to do their part in "preserving Jerusalem...the effort to preserve Jerusalem cannot afford to wait or be delayed".
"Every day that passes is being exploited by the Israelis to create new facts, utilising the huge donations of wealthy Jews across the world," he said.
Israeli bulldozers last month started breaking ground to build Jewish housing on the outskirts of East Jerusalem, provoking violence and widespread Palestinian anger.

The company hopes to discourage Arab citizens of Jerusalem from emigrating because of economic hardship by creating jobs and setting up investment ventures including housing units and hotels. It would also renovate existing property and aimed to buy up prime real estate.
The Palestinian official in charge of Jerusalem, Faisal al-Husseini, who addressed the investor gathering, appealed for money to help thwart Israel's plans to change the Arab nature of the city.
"Investments in Jerusalem will help increase income and create jobs and channel new funds in housing which we have a desperate shortage of," Husseini said.
Investors also hope the company will act as a counterweight to Jewish groups aggressively trying to buy land in East Jerusalem, annexed by Israel after its capture in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.

"We have been shocked by the situation in Jerusalem...we have found that setting up a company to help our people in Jerusalem and buy and build and develop Arab property is one of the urgent steps needed to resist Israeli plans," said Munib al-Masri, one of the three businessmen behind the company.

Organisers said $100 million was raised on Saturday from some of the 250 Palestinian expatriate and local investors, including top Jordanian and Palestinian banks and firms, who attended and gave their commitments to the first seed money.
Shareholders will be asked to pay initially 20 percent of the capital as soon as it is formally launched.
